llm.summary: This skill is a legitimate planning helper, but it asks for broad automatic activation and persistent learning from user tasks, including optional memory-log mining, without enough scoping or disclosure.

dimensions.detail: Semantic splitting, template matching, model downloads, and JSON template management fit the stated planning purpose, but the artifacts also describe scheduled extraction from memory logs and automatic conversion of task history into reusable templates, which goes beyond ordinary request decomposition.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases are very broad everyday Chinese requests, and the planning prompt permits slight hard-constraint violations in the divergent plan. Those instructions increase the chance of accidental routing or unsafe planning behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Quick-start and helper scripts include package installation and Hugging Face model downloads, while the permissions document claims no network or subprocess use. The operations are not inherently unsafe, but the capability disclosure is inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill writes reusable JSON templates and documents scheduled scanning of capabilities and recent memory logs. That persistence and historical-data access are high-impact compared with a planning-only skill unless explicitly opted into.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: JSON helpers can read or write user-supplied paths, and the workflow describes saving generated capability templates for future reuse. There is no clear consent gate, redaction policy, overwrite protection, or confinement to the declared data directory in all helper paths.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a planning skill that may build and reuse local JSON templates from tasks. Avoid enabling scheduled memory-log processing unless you explicitly want historical interactions mined into templates, and review any package installs, model downloads, and JSON write paths before running the helper scripts.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in substance: model downloads and setup commands are visible in the skill, but the low/no-network/no-subprocess permission claims do not match those artifacts.
[TP4] expected: Partially downgraded: setup, model download, and JSON management are coherent support functions for semantic matching, but they are under-disclosed relative to the simple planning presentation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the automation reference: scheduled processing of memory logs and bulk artifact generation materially expands data access and persistence beyond normal semantic splitting.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for path handling and memory-derived artifacts: local JSON helpers accept arbitrary paths, and documented memory-log transformation could retain sensitive historical task content.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: triggers such as common requests to do or analyze something are too broad for a skill that can scan templates and persist derived plans.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: the self-enhancing loop and template writes are disclosed, but not paired with clear per-run user consent, redaction, review, or deletion controls.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted as a review concern: the divergent planning prompt allows slight hard-constraint breaking, even though later rules also call for constraint checks.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted for the heavyweight automation task: turning memory logs into generalized reusable JSON can preserve private operational context even if obvious secrets are not copied verbatim.
[SSD-4] unexpected: Accepted as an instruction-quality concern rather than malicious behavior: the planning text normalizes constraint relaxation in one sub-plan.
